yomu reads .epub, .txt, and DRM-free .mobi and .azw3 books on a jailbroken Kindle (Paperwhite 2 and newer).

Needs the jailbreak hotfix that exposes /dev/fb0, plus KUAL (firmware
before 5.16.3) or KUALA (5.16.3 and later).

Copy onto the Kindle USB drive:

  yomu/                 -> the root of the USB drive
  extensions/yomu/      -> extensions/ on the USB drive

Eject, open KUAL or KUALA, and choose yomu. The yomu item pauses the
Kindle UI. yomu no framework stops it and starts it again on
exit. Put .epub, .txt, .mobi, and .azw3 files in yomu/books on the USB drive. .azw is the same container. Encrypted, fixed-layout, and KFX files stay unopened. yomu
creates that folder if it is missing. yomu starts in landscape, turned 90
degrees (1648x1236 on a Paperwhite 11), and typesets each page to that panel.
That orientation is fixed.

Swipe down from the top of the library and choose 転送. A browser on the same Wi-Fi can upload
and download files in yomu/books. A .ttf, .ttc, .otf, or .otc upload is stored in yomu/fonts, and the page lists that folder. Open 文字 to use the face. The screen shows http://yomu.local/
(or http://yomu.local:8080/ when 80 is busy) and the numeric address.
There is no password. Tap 戻る to leave the screen. The server keeps
running until yomu exits.
It uses port 80, or 8080 if 80 is busy. Set YOMU_PORT to force one
port. Connect Wi-Fi first, and launch yomu so Wi-Fi stays up.
yomu no framework can drop the network.

This package has been used on a Paperwhite 11. See the README in the source
tree for touch and viewport overrides if the picture or taps are wrong.
Log: yomu/yomu.log on the Kindle drive.
